stemMd: Suppose the additional condition is: Origins must be in position 1. Which further statement must then be true?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Origins must not be in position 1.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Origins and Legacy must not occupy consecutive positions.

explanationMd:
First restrict attention to orders satisfying the extra condition as well as the original rules. There are 4 such orders. "Origins and Legacy must not occupy consecutive positions." holds throughout this restricted set; the other statements fail on the explicit examples in their feedback.

The remaining orders are:
- Origins → Trade → Ritual → Legacy → Change
- Origins → Trade → Legacy → Ritual → Change
- Origins → Change → Ritual → Legacy → Trade
- Origins → Change → Legacy → Ritual → Trade

distractorRationale.c: Even with the additional condition, Origins → Trade → Ritual → Legacy → Change is permitted and makes this statement false.

Additional condition: Origins must be in position 1 leave 4 valid orders: Origins>Trade>Ritual>Legacy>Change; Origins>Trade>Legacy>Ritual>Change; Origins>Change>Ritual>Legacy>Trade; Origins>Change>Legacy>Ritual>Trade.
